title: Israel's Secret Iraq Desert Base Fueled Iran Air War
excerpt: A WSJ report reveals Israel built a covert military outpost in Iraq — without Baghdad's knowledge — to sustain its strikes on Iran.
body:
A Wall Street Journal investigation published May 9 has exposed one of the most audacious covert military operations of the Iran conflict: Israel secretly built and defended a forward operating base deep in the Iraqi desert to support its aerial campaign against Tehran — all without Baghdad's knowledge or consent.

**What Israel Built:**
Israel established the clandestine outpost shortly before US-Israeli strikes on Iran commenced on February 28, with Washington's knowledge but not Iraq's approval. The installation served as a logistics hub for the Israeli Air Force, housed special forces units, and stationed search-and-rescue teams ready to recover any downed Israeli pilots over Iranian territory. Military analysts told the Journal that Iraq's vast, sparsely populated western desert made it an ideal site to position assets significantly closer to Iranian territory.

**How It Nearly Unraveled:**
In early March, a local shepherd reported 'unusual military activity' — including helicopters and gunfire — to Iraqi state media, prompting Iraqi troops to investigate. Israel responded with airstrikes that killed one Iraqi soldier and drove the units back. Baghdad initially blamed Washington for the strikes, filing a formal complaint with the United Nations, but sources cited by the Journal confirmed the US had no involvement. Then-Israeli Air Force chief Maj. Gen. Tomer Bar had hinted at something extraordinary, saying his special units were 'carrying out extraordinary missions that can spark one's imagination' — without elaborating further.

**What to Watch:**
With US-Iran nuclear negotiations potentially resuming in Islamabad as early as next week, how Iraq — caught between its US security ties and Tehran-backed factions within its own borders — responds to this sovereignty breach will shape the region's next chapter.

sources.label: The Wall Street Journal (via Times of Israel)

nri_angle: Indian-Americans with family ties to Gulf states and business interests linked to oil markets should watch closely: the Strait of Hormuz disruptions triggered by this conflict have already rattled global energy prices, and further escalation could hit remittance corridors and trade flows that the diaspora depends on.
